summary: How British colonization of India's Andaman Islands from 1857, through a penal colony, abductions, disease and coercive administrators like Maurice Portman, devastated the islanders, and why the Sentinelese still reject all contact.
keywords: The Last Island of the Savages

notes: Primary subject treated as the place; the Andamanese peoples as a whole could also be an ethnic-group primary. genocide-mass-killing kept secondary despite the deaths being largely unintended, since the title frames it so and village burnings occur. Marco Polo and the 1771 sighting are brief background, so covered_span starts at 1857. main_span end 1900 approximates the end of Portman's tenure.
